title: Shivaji's Escape From Agra
text:
In 1665, after a Mughal army under Jai Singh pressed him hard, the Maratha leader Shivaji agreed to the Treaty of Purandar, giving up many forts. Jai Singh then persuaded him to travel north to the court of the emperor Aurangzeb at Agra, with assurances of his safety.

Shivaji arrived with his young son Sambhaji in May 1666, around the time of the emperor's birthday celebrations. At the audience he was placed among nobles of lower rank than he expected. Accounts agree that he showed his anger openly in the hall. Soon he found himself under house arrest, his residence surrounded by guards, while the court debated what to do with him.

Shivaji did not try to force his way out. He sent most of his men home, which reduced suspicion, and declared himself ill. He began sending large baskets of sweets and food out of the house as gifts to holy men and nobles, and the guards grew used to checking them less and less. In August 1666, according to the traditional account, Shivaji and Sambhaji slipped out hidden in the baskets, while a servant lay in Shivaji's bed with only his hand and ring showing. The escape was discovered only hours later.

Shivaji traveled back to the Deccan in disguise, leaving Sambhaji hidden with trusted people at Mathura, and eventually reached his own lands safely. Within a few years he recovered the forts he had surrendered, and in 1674 he was crowned king.
lesson: When force is impossible, patience and routine can be your tools. Let watchers grow used to a pattern, then use it.
source: Jadunath Sarkar, Shivaji and His Times (1919); Mughal and Maratha chronicles
caveat: The details of the escape, including the baskets, come from traditional accounts and are not certain.
